Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-21
Start: 14:30 PST
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Lina Gomez (CSM) -- Markus Feld (Halcyon Procurement), Aisha Rahman (InfoSec), Liam Ortiz (Platform Eng), Priya Kapoor (Legal)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
- Discussed MSA/DPA redline expectations, privileged access and KMS integration, SLA targets for Hosted vs Dedicated, and next steps for pilot + security artifacts.
- Action items and dates captured; legal follow-up requested.

Topics detected: onboarding playbook; data classification & privileged access; SLA tiers and latency/cost tradeoffs; KMS/SSO integration; MSA/DPA exceptions; pilot scope and benchmarks.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about 45 minutes, so we'll try to cover the onboarding playbook, the legal redlines, and then Ethan will walk through the pilot plan.
[00:18] Markus (Halcyon): Great, thanks. Quick context — procurement timeline is end of Q1, but security needs must be cleared before procurement committee signs off. So we need clarity on privileged access and the DPA.
[00:36] Aisha (InfoSec): Hi — we will need SOC2 and the pen test, and a clear KMS story. Also data classification — are logs or prompts stored? retention periods?
[00:52] Maya: Yes, we'll share SOC2/ISO artifacts. For logs, Redwood hosted keeps ephemeral logs by default, but customers can opt-in for retention; we'll send the DPA section that covers retention windows. Note: tradeoff across retention and auditability.
[01:12] Priya (Legal): On the MSA we have three asks — limitation of liability carveouts, data redaction SLA, and breach notification timelines. We'll send specifics after this call.
[01:27] Ethan (Redwood SE): On the technical side, for Halcyon use case, we recommend either Hosted with private routes or Dedicated capacity. Dedicated gives predictable latency for high-volume payments flows; Hosted is faster to go-live. Also we support VPC peering and customer-managed KMS via our private offering.
[01:55] Liam (Platform Eng): Can you clarify KMS? We want to manage keys via our cloud K M S provider, and ensure tokens never leave our control.
[02:10] Ethan: Yes, you can integrate customer K M S via Redwood Private. There's an HSM/KMS integration doc — we'll share. Small note: some customers call it kay-ems or K M S, autocaptures sometimes wrong.
[02:30] Speaker 1 (Maya): quick Q on SLAs — is 95th p99 supported? sorry, p99 or p95?
[02:40] Ethan: We target p95 SLOs in Hosted for short sequences; Dedicated can be tuned to reduce p99 variance. Example: for 1k tokens sequences we see median 120ms, p95 210ms on Dedicated pools — but that's model and token-length dependent. We'll include the benchmark spreadsheet.
[03:05] Markus: Cost vs latency is the big tradeoff. Procurement wants unit economics. How does Redwood report token costs? Token-level cost breakdown?
[03:20] Maya: Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdown by route and model. For high-volume flows we recommend batching and KV cache; that reduces per-token cost but can increase tail latency for single-shot requests.
[03:40] Aisha: Cache is worrying for us — if KV cache persists sensitive prefixes, that could violate our data retention policy. What's the default?
[03:55] Ethan: Default cache is ephemeral per request, but we have prefix caching features that can be disabled. For PCI-like data we recommend disabling prefix cache and using strict prompt redaction. We'll share configuration options and the best practice playbook.
[04:15] Priya: Can we get a clause in the DPA that says Redwood will not persist payment-card numbers and will scrub PII from logs?
[04:27] Maya: We can propose language. We need to align on what Halcyon considers PII — we'll ask Priya for the list.
[04:40] Liam: On connectivity, we need VPC peering and egress controls. Also curious: does Redwood Dedicated support auto-scaling within a commit? If we overrun burst capacity what happens?
[04:55] Ethan: Dedicated supports autoscaling policies; burst capacity is optional and billed differently. If you commit reserved capacity, we can set fallback routes to hosted variants in emergencies. That's in the routing policy section of the onboarding playbook.
[05:15] Maya: We'll include the routing/fallback play in the deck.
[05:25] Speaker 2 (Markus): about procurement — our gating questions: 1) Do you have SSO options (SAML)? 2) K M S integration for private keys? 3) Price floor for Dedicated?
[05:40] Maya: Yes on SAML/SSO and RBAC, yes on customer K M S for Private, and we'll give price range for Dedicated based on GPU family and qps. I'll get finance to produce two scenarios.
[05:58] Ethan: Technically, if you choose quantized model variants we can reduce GPU cost by ~30% but you might see subtle quality differences for certain prompts; we'll run evals with your prompt set.
[06:20] Aisha: On the pen-test — will Redwood accept our third-party assessor to run a targeted test?
[06:30] Lina (CSM): We have an onboarding process for third-party testing; typical cadence is an NDA + scanning windows, and we coordinate with infra. We'll share the intake form.
[06:44] Priya: On MSA redlines, our legal prefers enumerated indemnities and a 30-day breach notice. Is Redwood flexible?
[06:55] Maya: We'll take back the redlines. For breach notification we have standard 72-hour notify requirement in our base MSA; exceptions can be discussed but will require exec approval.
[07:10] Markus: Procurement needs a clear list of artifacts to sign off — what do you require?
[07:18] Maya: Typical: MSA+DPA executed, SOC2 or ISO attestation, pen-test report, SSO/KMS confirmation, pilot results for latency and functional correctness on your prompts, and an agreed SLA.
[07:34] Markus: Ok. Let's talk pilot scope — Ethan?
[07:38] Ethan: Plan: 1) 1-week isolated pilot on a Dedicated trial or Hosted private route; 2) run 3 benchmark suites — latency, throughput, regression for prompt set; 3) observe cost and error rates. Deliverables: benchmark spreadsheet, sample logs, config snippets. We'll need a small corpus of prompts (approx 100) and expected outputs.
[08:02] Liam: We can provide prompt set and test harness. We prefer Dedicated for latency stability but open to Hosted if it expedites timeline.
[08:15] Maya: We'll propose both pilot paths and recommend Dedicated if latency is critical.
[08:22] Aisha: Also need to confirm network egress and data residency — our legal requires EU-only storage for EU customers. Does Redwood support region pinning?
[08:35] Ethan: Yes, region pinning and local model variants supported for Private and Dedicated. For Hosted we have region options but data may route within region boundaries; DPA notes specifics.
[08:50] Priya: any export control language — we handle cross-border data?
[08:55] Maya: We'll include data residency clauses in the DPA; we'll add export-control references for review.
[09:05] Speaker 3 (Priya): Also, pricing approval board wants a committed term. What's typical? 6-12 months?
[09:13] Maya: Dedicated commitments typically 12 months for reserved capacity; we can do pilots shorter. Pricing flexes with term and commit.
[09:22] Markus: Ok that helps.
[09:28] Ethan: One note — when customers run embedding workloads vs. chat generation, cost and kernel choice differ. We'll map your main workloads to model variants in the pilot.
[09:40] Liam: We use embeddings for fraud detection — large batch jobs overnight — how is that priced?
[09:47] Maya: Embeddings have a separate unit metric; we can include batch pricing in the spreadsheet. For overnight batch, Dedicated with scheduled nodes is efficient.
[09:58] Aisha: About logging — can we get audit logs to our SIEM? Event-level?
[10:05] Ethan: Yes, event logs and request/response metadata can be forwarded; full content may be masked by default. We'll provide logging integration guides (syslog/Cloud Pub/Sub/etc).
[10:20] Markus: Great. Questions from legal?
[10:25] Priya: On limitation of liability — can we get a carveout for gross negligence and willful misconduct?
[10:33] Maya: Standard is mutual carveouts. We'll take your redline and flag any executive approvals needed.
[10:40] Priya: Also want clarity on subprocessor list.
[10:45] Lina: We'll attach the current subprocessor list; note that it's updated quarterly.
[10:52] Ethan: Technical caveat — if you use on-prem/private deployment there are ops responsibilities around patching, but Redwood provides an ops playbook.
[11:05] Liam: Is there a vault-ready integration for secrets?
[11:09] Ethan: Yes: HashiVault, AWS Secrets Manager, and GCP Secret Manager supported for key rotation; we'll provide sample configs.
[11:20] Speaker 1 (Maya): OK, let's move to recap and commitments.
[11:25] Maya: Recap: Redwood to send MSA/DPA redline + suggested language for retention and breach notice; Lina to share SOC2/pen-test; Ethan to propose pilot plan and spreadsheet; Maya to assemble pricing scenarios and bring finance into the thread. Priya to send legal exceptions list.
[11:45] Markus: Timeline check — can we get an initial package by next week? Procurement meets on 2025-12-02.
[11:55] Maya: We'll aim for sending the package by 2025-11-28.
[12:05] Priya: One more — can Redwood accept a small indemnity cap increase if we commit 12 months?
[12:12] Maya: We'll take that to our legal team and respond in the redline.
[12:20] Aisha: For the pilot, we prefer Dedicated trial to mirror production.
[12:25] Ethan: Noted — we'll prepare a Dedicated trial plan and cost estimate.
[12:33] Liam: We'll share prompt corpus and infra details before the workshop.
[12:40] Maya: Great, we'll follow up with a shared folder and a short timeline.
[12:48] Lina: I'll drop SOC2 & pen-test links.
[12:55] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll schedule the legal triage call once Priya shares redlines.
[13:05] Markus: Thanks — talk soon.
